reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the redline is byte-identical to the original with no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited language in Section 9.2(b) runs in our favour (Array cannot force Ono to order directly from a Subcontractor unless that Subcontractor offers Ono terms as favourable as those given to Array), i.e. comparable-terms protection benefiting Customer, which the rule expressly says to mark compliant and not redline.
No MFN-style undertaking by Ono to extend better third-party terms to Array or to match third-party offers is present in the cited text, supporting the preferred position (no MFN burden on Customer).
The rationale appropriately notes the Section 8.2 exclusivity covenants as a distinct commercial term rather than double-flagging them under this rule.
